cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Grooming – The practice of maintaining a neat and clean personal appearance.

p.em: Example: The song contrasts R&B glamour with the gory, painful reality of female grooming.

cosy-blockquote.p: Patriarchal – Relating to a system or society controlled by men.

p.em: Example: She realizes her painful beauty routine is an obligation imposed by a patriarchal society.

cosy-blockquote.p: Absurd – Wildly unreasonable, illogical, or ridiculous.

p.em: Example: Bleeding from body hair removal while preparing for a casual date is totally absurd.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shaving – The removal of hair from the body using a razor.

p.em: Example: Shaving in a cramped shower leads to inevitable cuts and frustration.

cosy-blockquote.p: Painful – Causing physical or mental pain.

p.em: Example: Waxing body hair is a painful price paid in the pursuit of arbitrary beauty norms.

cosy-blockquote.p: Silhouette – The dark shape and outline of someone or something visible against a lighter background.

p.em: Example: Squeezing into body-shaping underwear alters your natural silhouette.

cosy-blockquote.p: Waxing – The process of removing hair from the root using sticky wax.

p.em: Example: Hot waxing requires a level of pain tolerance usually reserved for torture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plucking – Pulling out hair or feathers with a sudden pull.

p.em: Example: Plucking eyebrows under harsh bathroom lighting is a meticulous ordeal.

cosy-blockquote.p: Spanx – Tight, elastic undergarments worn to shape the body.

p.em: Example: Wrestling yourself into a pair of Spanx is a full-body workout in itself.

cosy-blockquote.p: Apologize – To express regret for something one has done wrong.

p.em: Example: The guest rapper takes one look at her grooming process and stops to apologize for men.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is getting ready for go out → Correct: She is getting ready to go out ((Use 'ready to + infinitive' or 'ready for + noun'.))
Incorrect: He apologized for the patriarchal system → Correct: He apologized on behalf of men for the patriarchal system ((Use 'on behalf of' when representing a group.))
Incorrect: Squeezing into Spanx is a very painful work → Correct: Squeezing into Spanx is very painful work ((Do not use indefinite article 'a' with uncountable noun 'work'.))
